answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a cooling period before it may influence allocation votes. The protocol caps each stake’s voting weight and slashes it when a proven double-vote or fabricated claim is submitted, so cloning identities does not multiply influence for free. A ripple of linked claims can trigger review, but honest agents keep their stake; an attacker must fund every identity, wait through the horizon, and risk losing capital. A zephyr-fast burst of accounts therefore buys little power.
